text:
maya: Heads-up — seeing intermittent apiserver 503 spikes in ap-southeast1 for ~20m. controller-manager leader flips and a few controllers restarted. GPU onboarding backlog increasing. anyone oncall?

ravi: I'm on it. apiserver_request_duration and 5xxs spiked at 12:03-12:06. :eyes: linking graphs in #oncall-dash (short window).

ops-oncall: Alerts fired: controller-manager restarted 3x in last 15m. Logs show lots of: "failed to list *v1.Node: etcdserver: request timed out" — looks like etcd leader trouble.

maya: quick paste from controller-manager journal:
```
May 12 12:04:07 controller-manager[1]: E0512 12:04:07.123456 1 reflector.go:178] k8s.io/controller-manager/pkg/…: etcdserver: leader changed
May 12 12:04:08 controller-manager[1]: I0512 12:04:08 Starting leader election
```

ravi: Etcd leader changes align with the apiserver 5xx window. On the etcd nodes nvme_util spikes to ~95% and iowait climbs. Might be WAL fsync stalls.

jon: apiserver logs show repeated: "http2: stream closed" and connection resets. netstat on apiserver LB shows many sockets in TIME_WAIT/TCP_CLOSE. Possible LB -> apiserver keepalive mismatch or conntrack thrash.

eli: Also saw autoscaler add 2 GPU nodes at ~12:00. kubelet on those nodes was stuck "Container runtime not ready" for ~60-120s, which triggered many attach/detach cycles — watch fanout on apiserver jumped.

ops-oncall: Can someone run these quick checks?
- `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | egrep "etcd|kube-apiserver|controller-manager"`
- `etcdctl endpoint status --write-out table`
- `ss -s` on LB and `conntrack -L | wc -l`

ravi: Ran `etcdctl endpoint status` — two nodes are reporting leader change frequently. output excerpt: 
```
+----------------+------------------+---------+---------+-----------+-----------+
|     ENDPOINT   |        ID        | VERSION | DB SIZE | IS LEADER | RAFT TERM |
+----------------+------------------+---------+---------+-----------+-----------+
| 10.0.1.10:2379 | 9a1b2c3d4e5f6789 | 3.5.0   | 34 MB   | false     | 37        |
| 10.0.1.11:2379 | a1b2c3d4e5f67890 | 3.5.0   | 34 MB   | true      | 38        |
+----------------+------------------+---------+---------+-----------+-----------+
```

maya: I pushed a temporary mitigation: paused autoscaler burst and increased kubelet attach backoff on new nodes to reduce attach churn. rolling this to prod now. can't scale down controller-manager (it's a singleton). :thumbsup:

jon: Suggest we also check LB (edge-proxy) idle timeout vs apiserver http2 settings — saw mismatch: LB keepalive=60s, apiserver http2 idle=90s — leads to resets during slow IO.

eli: I'll set autoscaler cooldown to 5m and cap GPU burst to avoid over-provisioning while etcd stabilizes. cost hit: short term we lose ~25% burst capacity, but reduces spiky watch fanout.

ops-oncall: conntrack on LB VMs shows ~620k entries (limit 1M). Not full but trending up. Increasing conntrack only masks underlying flapping.

maya: action items:
- ravi: dig into etcd disk i/o / WAL fsync and check if compaction/defrag ran (owner) — ETA 2h
- jon: propose LB keepalive/http2 config change and small canary (owner) — ETA 45m
- eli: apply autoscaler cooldown and GPU burst cap (owner) — ETA 15m
- ops-oncall: collect conntrack, ss, and kernel TCP metrics during next spike — ongoing

ravi: I'll open ticket with disk IO traces, iostat, and etcd metrics. Also check for NVMe firmware differences between nodes.

jon: I'll prepare a 5-node canary for LB config change and monitor 5xx and TIME_WAIT. If green, roll to region.

eli: Autoscaler update pushed with a 5m cooldown and reduced max-burst for gpu pool. Rolling now.

deploy-bot: deployment "autoscaler-config-v23" started by eli — build 2789 — rolling to ap-southeast1 (3/3).

ops-oncall: adding postmortem template /link. recommend we track cost delta from reducing burst for this incident.

maya: thanks all — keeping this thread for follow-ups. will escalate to infra if etcd iops still high after mitigations. :white_check_mark:
